body: Reset Ends is an option for cases where StateMachines are nested, allowing you to blend the animation outside the nest with the animation inside AFAIR. If an unintended T-pose occurs when Reset Ends is disabled, I believe it means the blend amount is set to 0, but the cause requires investigation. > While the above is reproducible, I've found this T pose to randomly occur when leaving any nested Root state machine with a similar configuration often, even when by all accounts unwarranted. Since Nested type statemachine identify dead ends as endpoints, disconnecting the connection to End in this image should result in the intended behavior, how about it? (When not using termination checks based on connection priority) In summary, I think the issue is that animations with a blend amount of 0 are processed, and if they are determined to be currently playing, other queues are not processed in the parent statemachine. In cases where the blend amount was 1 in at least the previous frame, and the blend amount becomes 0 on the frame where the animation's termination is determined, I assume we should avoid it.

> Since Nested type statemachine identify dead ends as endpoints, disconnecting the connection to End in this image should result in the intended behavior, how about it? (When not using termination checks based on connection priority)

That's a whole other problem, unfortunately. If I was to delete every one of the `At End` transitions to `End`, the fact that "static" and 
"moving" have sync commitments to one another would make the `Nested` StateMachine _never_ leave itself, even though the conditions to sync to either never occur. Unfortunately, this is somehow #114109 again, at a nested level, preventing exit. They inherently commit to sync even with a failing advance condition, and therefore never allow an exit.

Hey! I've put together a potential fix for the Rest-pose flicker when exiting nested AnimationNodeStateMachines. It definitely solves the minimal example you sent. You can see it in the video I attached.

Since this is just my initial idea for a fix, **it would be great if someone could run this through a test suite** if you have one, just to make sure it holds up in other cases too! You can find the fix in my  [godot fork](https://github.com/spinalcord/spinal-godot/commit/7a8c406c8ea01a5e247702b9d6aeccfbed379d5f).  

JUST a heads-up that I am NOT a Godot engine dev, I really just put this together to get it working for my own project.

The Idea:
I introduced a "ghost frame" mechanism. When a nested state machine hits its End node, it now holds the last rendered state frozen at full weight to bridge the transition into the parent blend. This prevents it from falling back to a rest pose.

Some details on the implementation:
- animation_node_state_machine.cpp and animation_node_state_machine.h
- It tracks the last_rendered_state as a fallback for quick transitions (like multi-hop chains in one tick).
- It avoids using Start as a fade source since it has no animation to render. Other intermediate hops in the same tick are still used as ghosts, they're blended live via blend_node(), so suppressing their xfade would break valid SYNC/cross-fade transitions on multi-hop travel paths.
- It skips _clear_fading at the End node so the ghost survives until the parent takes over.

Edit **Me from the future**: Unfortunately, this approach can lead to unexpected behavior in some cases. If you need a quick solution, its ok. However, switching back to the master branch may result in incompatibilities. Atm I would use godots `travel` and `start` feature inside a gd script to avoid the rest pose flicker.
